_about: Every parameter of the router table (#6740), read by build.py. Data, not code: change a number here and re-run. A route's outcome is acceptance judged against the page image (route-judge pilot, #7376), not agreement with Opus. Opus is the judge, not the reference reader. The hierarchical models (v1, v2) give only the weak prior.

prior._about: Acceptance prior per route. Draft served as-is: v1's P(passes the absolute floors) for the draft engine in its chart. Draft plus corrector: d + (1 - d) x v2's median net gain for that corrector in that cell (d = the draft's prior mean, 0.5 if v1 has no chart). Worth pages_measured pages (a + b) when every input is measured, pages_pooled when any is pooled. Flat Beta(1, 1) where neither model covers the route (translation, Tibetan drafts).
prior._learned: 2026-10-28 (#7263, job router-backfill-all-7263; fit_prior.py, was 4 / 2 by hand). Empirical Bayes over the 15 tested routes whose prior comes from v1 / v2: route acceptance ~ Beta(m W, (1 - m) W), the book-scaled judged k of n beta-binomial around it. Maximum marginal likelihood W = 7.0 pages, profile 90% [3.5, 14.5], route bootstrap [3.4, 25.8]. Measured and pooled priors fitted apart give 4.3 [1.4, 12.5] and 10.5 [4.1, 29.2]; the split gains 0.52 log-likelihood for one more parameter, so one weight for both (the data do not say pooled priors are worse). Calibration: logit(acceptance) = 1.2 + 0.40 [0.20, 0.60] x logit(prior mean): the prior predicts the order of routes but its means are too extreme and too low. One route carries most of the misfit: Latin Flash-Lite, v1 0.035 (P(passes the absolute CER floors)) against 0.65 judged; without it W = 14.9. Refit after each backfill: python3 scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/fit_prior.py <table>.json.
prior._v1_charts_left_out: German and French OCR have no v1 chart: latin-script-other is web-transcribed text and gives Flash-Lite 0.998, against 17/30 the judge accepted on Latin. Chinese print: v1 says its floors measure the reference panel's variant forms.

calibration.why: Fitted 2026-10-28 (fit_prior.py, 15 tested routes, book-scaled): logit(acceptance) = 1.12 + 0.38 x logit(v1/v2 mean), W 16.9 pages. It fails its held-out check: leaving one CELL out, the held-out log likelihood is -205.3 calibrated against -202.1 uncalibrated, and |prior mean - observed| 0.139 against 0.119; without Latin Flash-Lite's draft (v1 0.035 against 0.65 judged, the route that makes the slope) -191.6 against -184.3. An intercept-only shift (+0.36 logit, W 10) is a wash held out (-202.7 against -202.1; MAE 0.109 against 0.119). So the uncalibrated prior stays in force and the calibration is shown as a sensitivity; refit after each backfill.

script_split._about: Derek, 2026-10-28 11:54Z (job inbox, router-next-7263): 'do we distinguish between manuscript and print? ... because we must ... might need to recalculate.' Every cell is split by the SCRIPT TYPE of its pages (build.py expand_by_script): <id>/print, <id>/manuscript, <id>/unknown. A judged page's type: the <script> tag of its current OCR where pages.script_type is missing, the tag on a conflict, else the field, else its book's majority, else unknown (reported apart, never pooled); mixed counts as print (scripts/eval/router-next-7263/script-type.mjs). Evidence: the same sources cut per page (split_evidence.py, every source reconciled page by page first). Pages waiting: the cell's count x the share waiting-split.mjs measured on its books. A manuscript cell takes no v1/v2 prior (fitted on print), and with fewer than min_manuscript_pages judged pages on every route it says UNTESTED / HOLD rather than inheriting print numbers; so does an unknown-script cell (its prior is print's). --no-script-split builds the table unsplit.

_cluster_note: The judge's pages are not independent within a book. When a route's n pages come from fewer books (Latin: 30 pages in 9 books), k and n are scaled by books / n before they enter the posterior. Wrong-text pages are read as the page count k of n.

evidence_rules._about: Which earlier tests enter, and how (#7263 backfill-all, 2026-10-28; the 214 judged write-ups are classified on #7263). (1) Instrument: per-page verdicts against the page IMAGE, by an Opus judge, that split accept from wrong text (route-judge accept / wrong_text; Step T or Step C misleading; judge.py MISLEADING; MQM material; a serious-error flag). A 1-5 or 0-5 score, a CER or accuracy against a typed reference, and a better / same / worse judgment do not enter: the first two feed the v1 / v2 priors where they feed anything. A Gemini-only judge does not enter (#6561: 5 of 5 of its 'invented' calls checked by eye were printed text). (2) The frame: pages drawn as the lane draws them; a set selected FOR difficulty (disagreement, changed pages, a CER bin, a detector flag) does not enter. (3) Stored per-page verdicts in the repo; counts quoted only in a write-up do not enter. (4) A test of another prompt or model than the route's enters as ITS OWN route (never an Opus arm: switch.bar) (Arabic: the #6544 diplomatic READ prompt is agy-flash-low-read-diplomatic, not agy-flash-low-read). (5) The same route measured under another prompt or model vintage than the one that made, or will make, the cell's pages enters at `weight` (below) of its books: a fresh Flash-Lite read standing in for the stored lite drafts (#6553, #7341). (6) Sources drawn from the same books form one `book_group`, scaled together by the group's books / its pages, so no book counts twice (the pilot's 30 Latin pages are 30 of #5924's 250). (7) Every judged reading of a route counts once; a reading a packet copied from an earlier step does not count again (#5924 Step C2 / C4).

switch._about: Reference = the measured route with the highest posterior mean acceptance (with bar = opus: the best measured Opus route, and Opus routes are never picked; see _bar). Pick the cheapest measured route with P(acc_route >= acc_reference - within) >= p AND wrong-text pages / n <= wrong_text_max. The pick is the current route: keep. Another route: switch. None qualifies: keep.
switch._bar: Derek, 2026-10-28 11:24Z (job inbox, router-backfill-all-7263): 'the route search is agy Gemini CLI and GPU routes ONLY. Opus is the judge and the bar to match, never a candidate route: add no Opus read, correction or translation arm, and recommend only agy/GPU routes (or keep the served route if none clears the bar).' So: the gate's reference is the best measured Opus route (the best measured route when the cell has none), the candidates are the other routes, and when none passes the cell keeps its current route. HOLD names the best candidate. Unset (or any other value) = the rule before: every measured route a candidate.
switch._within: 2026-10-28 (Derek: 'prioritize cost a bit more'): 0.05 -> 0.08, and wrong_text_max 0.02 -> 0.04. At 0.05/0.02 German Flash-Lite correction stayed on Opus although agy Flash-low tied it (28/30 each; wrong text 2/30 vs 1/30, one page). The new margins move that cell only; Latin lite (30/30 vs 24/30), German 3 Flash (29/29 vs 26/30), Chinese Paddle and Tibetan translation keep Opus because their gaps exceed them.
switch._wrong_text_bar: relative (Derek, 2026-10-26: cost is part of the measure): a route passes when its wrong-text rate is at most the best route's rate + wrong_text_max, so the cheaper of two equally good routes wins. absolute: at most wrong_text_max outright, which keeps the current route whenever every route misses 2% (Tibetan: 3/30 on both correctors). The other bar is reported as a sensitivity.
switch._pick: 2026-10-26b (Derek: 'and this takes cost into account?' -> 'yes'): among the routes that pass the gate, the pick is the lowest median expected dollars per ACCEPTED page, one unit for every channel (was: the lowest share of the channel's free week per RAW page). The margin is unchanged; sensitivity_within reports what a 0.10 margin would pick, flagged when that route is 0.05-0.10 below the best and >= sensitivity_cheaper times cheaper.
switch._bar_scope: Derek, 2026-10-28 12:06Z (job inbox, router-next-7263): 'I am assuming we need opus for manuscripts -- that is the plan ... at least for greek, maybe others measure ok.' So switch.bar = opus applies to PRINT (and unknown) cells only: in a MANUSCRIPT cell an Opus route is a candidate like any other, the gate's reference is the best measured route, and when no agy / GPU route clears it the router picks Opus. Greek manuscripts: Opus is the planned route (script_split.planned), no agy / GPU test needed to justify it.

_fallback_routes: A cell's `fallback_routes` run ONLY when their gate opens, never by the pick: build.py does not read them. agy-opus (#7545): Claude Opus through agy, allowed only on an account whose Gemini weekly bucket reads 0 and whose Claude buckets hold 10% (agyClaudeGate, scripts/lib/agy-cli.mjs). Each carries paired evidence against the cell's Opus route, the router's gate on it (switch.within, switch.p, the wrong-text bar), and its draw on the account's Claude group as a fraction per page (agy /quota before and after).

hold._about: HOLD when no measured route has P(acceptance >= hold.acc) >= hold.p.

test_next._about: score(cell) = max over routes that draw capacity of pages_waiting x share_per_page x Var(acceptance posterior); share_per_page = the route's draw per page / its channel's free week. A test is pages_per_test pages of each named route, plus one Opus judge call per output.
test_next.routes: the cell's untested routes; if every route is tested, the one with the largest share x variance

fees._about: Turns points and agy calls into dollars for the pick only. --fees <private fee file> (agy_month_usd, claude_usd_per_weekly_point; the file route_ocr_v1.py reads) when present; else every plan at default_plan_month_usd, the list price v2 and #7417 assumed. The source used is named in the table; dollar results go to stdout only, never into the repo.

size_model._about: Inbox 2026-10-26 17:21Z and 17:22Z (Derek: '10 pages are not the same in all books'; 'maybe 5 when it is multi column'). A Claude call costs k x (overhead + the tokens of each page in it), tokens weighted input + output_weight x output. Batching saves the overhead only: points per page = k x (overhead / pages per call + the page's own tokens). Page sizes per cell: page-size.mjs (draft characters, image pixels -> image tokens by Anthropic's resize rule, OCR <columns> tag). k is fitted from the meter readings below. The Claude weekly quota is NOT published per token: k is an estimate, and the spread of the readings is its range.
size_model._central: Central k per kind of call = the median of that kind's readings. The two image readings agree (pilot, correct.mjs); the translation lane's own reading implies a rate about 3x lower: less per-call overhead (no images to open) or the coarse integer meter. Pricing translation at the image rate would contradict its one direct measurement, so each kind keeps its own; the range spans all readings.
size_model._output_weight: Opus list price: output tokens cost 5x input. Assumes the weekly meter weighs them as the API price does (unpublished).

overhead.basis: the pilot's one-page Opus image call, 14.6K in / 1.5K out tokens (route-judge pilot meter), minus one page: image about 1.5K + draft about 0.7K tokens in, about 0.75K out. The rest is the claude -p system prompt, the instructions and the tool turns that open the files, paid once per call.

chars_per_token_default._basis: used where fewer than min_pages_for_measured_cpt pages record Gemini's output token count. Chinese and Tibetan: one token a character, a guess (Gemini's measured 1.56 on Chinese 3 Flash includes the tag markup). Claude's tokenizer differs from Gemini's; neither is measured here for Claude.

pages_per_call._basis: Derek 2026-10-26: 10 for single-column prose, 5 for multi-column pages (two-column print, tables, glossed or interlinear). A cell's effective figure mixes the two by its measured multi-column share (OCR <columns>N</columns> with N >= 2, self-reported, or page_type table). correct.mjs (--per-call, default 10) and claude-translate.mjs (--per-call=10) have no layout switch today: 5 for multi-column is the rule proposed here, not what the lanes do.

taxonomy: O1 confabulation (text not on the page); O4 block repetition; O5 silent omission; O6 meaning-changing misread; O7 numerals/dates wrong; O8 normalisation toward the expected; O10 secondary script dropped; O11 page furniture mis-tagged; O12 marginalia/apparatus dropped or mis-tagged; O16 self-reported tags wrong; I5 several leaves in one photo; T6 catchword/split-word seams; T8 sense inverted or qualifier dropped; T9 quiet omission; T10 invented scholarship in notes; T15 continuity meta wrong; E2 other.
